title: What You Call It
body:
# What You Call It

## A Field Guide to [[GLMZ]] Nomenclature

The three names for the zone function as a class-legibility test that nobody administers and everyone grades.

The first name is [[GLMZ]]. It appears on your transit card, your healthcare allocation ledger, your tier certification document, your employment contract if you have one, your residency filing if you are permitted to file one. [[GLMZ]] is the name that governance uses for the city because governance does not love the city and has never pretended to. The acronym was chosen by the [[GLMZ]] Economic Zone Authority in 2189, derived from the 88th meridian west — the longitudinal line designated as the zone's western civic consolidation boundary — and the letters arranged into [[GLMZ]]. [[The Reclamation Authority|The Authority]]'s communications division apparently did not notice this was phonetically identical to '[[GLMZ|Glooms]],' the affectionate-derogatory street name that residents of the old industrial districts had been using for the corridor for thirty years. This is either the greatest unintentional irony in the administrative history of [[Compass Rose|North]] America or a deliberate act of contempt dressed as incompetence. [[Soren Sokolov|Nobody]] who was in the room when the decision was made is talking.

Outsiders say [[GLMZ]]. Corp transplants on three-year rotational postings say [[GLMZ]]. Federal Remnant officials say [[GLMZ]]. Anyone whose relationship to the city is primarily professional, temporary, or extractive says [[GLMZ]]. The name is accurate and bloodless. It locates nothing, evokes nothing, belongs to nothing. It is an address, not a home.

## The Cultural Register

The second name is [[GLMZ|Meridian 88]].

This is the name that culture chose, in the years after the consolidation, when the zone's population had grown large [[Serenol|enough]] to need an identity that was not a bureaucratic designation. [[GLMZ|Meridian 88]] refers not to the zone's administrative boundary but to the infrastructure corridor built along the 88th meridian — the transit spines and data arteries and power grids that became the zone's nervous system, threading north from old [[Chicago]] through Milwaukee, [[Lambeau Terminus|Green Bay]], and into the Canadian frontier zone. The name spread through music first, then journalism, then commerce, then merchandise. By 2220 it was on every album released by an artist from the corridor, every cultural publication that covered the zone, every piece of aspirational graffiti on the [[Iron Meridian Cooperative Backbone IMC-3 'Spine'|Spine]]'s lower pylons. [[GLMZ|Meridian 88]] carries pride. It says: we are a place, not a designation. We have a name that we chose.

In everyday speech the name collapses: people say [[GLMZ|Meridian]], or [[GLMZ|The 88]], or M88. These are the same name in different registers — [[GLMZ|Meridian]] in the press, [[GLMZ|The 88]] in conversation, M88 in text and shorthand and transit spray. You learn these contractions not by being taught them but by being here long [[Serenol|enough]] that they become automatic. A tourist says '[[GLMZ|Meridian 88]].' A resident says '[[GLMZ|The 88]].' A lifer says '[[GLMZ|Meridian]]' — one word, no number, because if you live here you know which meridian.

The name is not neutral. It carries aspiration, which is a political position. To call the city [[GLMZ|Meridian 88]] is to claim that it is more than its administrative designation, that its culture and its people constitute something worth naming on their own terms. The corporations do not use it. The EZA does not use it. Which is, in its way, the point.

## The Street Register

The third name is the [[GLMZ|Glooms]].

This one requires no explanation if you have ever lived below Tier 3. The Great Lakes corridor runs grey and overcast for approximately 280 days a year. Lake-effect clouds roll in from Michigan and stack against the arcology towers until the sky is a permanent sealed ceiling. It rains sideways. It mists continuously when it is not raining. In the lower tiers, where structural canopies trap the weather and drainage systems have not been maintained since the 2190s, damp is not a description but a condition — your clothes, your walls, your lungs. The city is the [[GLMZ|Glooms]] because it looks like the glooms and it feels like the glooms and anyone who has lived here long [[Serenol|enough]] stops pretending otherwise.

Calling the city the [[GLMZ|Glooms]] is not bitterness. A corporate transplant who encounters the name assumes it is despairing, and this assumption marks them immediately as someone who does not understand what they are hearing. [[GLMZ|The Glooms]] is not despair. [[GLMZ|The Glooms]] is intimacy. It is the name you use for a place you know too well to romanticize. A person who loves someone [[SynapTech ReadRoom Social Cue Enhancer|tells]] the truth about them — their flaws, their contradictions, the way they look in bad light. A person who loves the city calls it the [[GLMZ|Glooms]] because they know it in bad light and have decided to stay anyway. A corporate executive would never say it. A lifer cannot say anything else.

## The [[Detroit]] Exception

There is a term that sits outside this taxonomy: [[Detroit]].

[[Detroit]] is inside [[GLMZ]]. [[Detroit]] residents are [[GLMZ]] citizens, their documentation carries [[GLMZ]] zone classification, and they are subject to [[GLMZ]] Economic Zone Authority jurisdiction. None of this is in dispute. What is incorrect — frequently assumed and consistently wrong — is that [[Detroit]] is part of [[GLMZ|Meridian 88]].

The 88th meridian corridor runs west of the lake, through the [[Chicago]]-Milwaukee-[[Lambeau Terminus|Green Bay]] spine. [[Detroit]] sits east of the lake, built on a different foundation, oriented toward a different economic history, culturally distinct from the western shore in ways that long predate the zone's formation. When a [[Detroit]] resident hears '[[GLMZ|Meridian 88]],' they know it means the western shore. When a western-shore resident uses '[[GLMZ|Meridian 88]],' they do not mean [[Detroit]]. This distinction is legally meaningless and socially absolute.

A [[Detroit]] resident asked if they are 'from the 88' will correct you. Some will do it gently. Some will not.

## The Grammar of Place

The three names are not interchangeable. They are not dialects of the same word. They are three separate relationships to the same geography, legible to anyone who knows how to read them.

[[GLMZ]] is a visitor. [[GLMZ|Meridian 88]] is a resident. [[GLMZ|The Glooms]] is someone who has nowhere else to go and has made their peace with it.

Every conversation in this city contains, in the first sentence someone speaks, a location signal — not what street, what district, what tier, but what relationship to the place. This signal is not performed. You cannot fake it. You either carry it or you don't, and the people who do know the difference the moment you open your mouth.

The corps say [[GLMZ]] because the city is an asset.

The residents say [[GLMZ|Meridian 88]] because the city is a home.

The excluded say the [[GLMZ|Glooms]] because the city is a fact.

All three of them are talking about the same 500 kilometers of concrete, steel, lake water, and human density. None of them mean quite the same thing.
headings: A Field Guide to GLMZ Nomenclature
